title: Hard Times and Faith That Acts
overview: James writes to scattered believers about facing hardship with endurance, asking God for wisdom, and showing their faith in how they actually live.

parts.label: Greeting to the scattered (v. 1)
parts.note: Tradition says this James was the brother of Jesus who led the early church in Jerusalem, though scholars debate who wrote the letter. He addresses the twelve tribes living abroad, which likely means Jewish followers of Jesus spread outside Israel, or possibly all believers pictured as God's people far from home.

parts.label: Joy and wisdom in trials (vv. 2-8)
parts.note: Hardships test faith the way fire tests metal, and enduring them builds a steady, mature character. Anyone lacking wisdom for this can ask God, who gives freely without scolding, but a person torn between trusting and not trusting is like a wave pushed around by the wind.

parts.label: Poor and rich (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: The poor believer can take pride in their worth before God, and the rich can take pride in being humbled, because wealth fades like a wildflower in a scorching wind, an image borrowed from Isaiah. Scholars are unsure whether the rich person here is meant as a fellow believer or an outsider.

parts.label: Testing versus temptation (vv. 12-18)
parts.note: The same Greek word can mean both "trial" and "temptation," and James insists God never lures anyone to evil; that pull comes from a person's own desires, which grow like a pregnancy into sin and finally death. Every good thing comes from God, who never shifts like a shadow, and believers are called firstfruits, the first part of a harvest offered to God, which many interpreters read as a sign of more to come for all creation.

parts.label: Listen, then do (vv. 19-25)
parts.note: James urges people to listen more than they talk and to let go of anger, because anger does not produce the good life God wants. Hearing God's message without living it is like glancing in a mirror and forgetting your own face, and the law James says brings freedom probably means God's teaching as Jesus taught it, followed willingly.

parts.label: What real religion looks like (vv. 26-27)
parts.note: Religious talk means little if a person cannot control their tongue. Real faith cares for orphans and widows, who in that world often had no protector or income, and stays free of the world's corrupting ways.

think: When has a hard stretch in your life changed you, and was the change for better, worse, or some of both?
